root.name: Semi-Slav Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 e6

overview: Black combines the Slav c6 with ...e6, building a sturdy centre at the cost of a locked c8 bishop. White's main tries are 5.Bg5 (Botvinnik and Anti-Moscow), 5.e3 (Meran and Stonewall-like set-ups) and 5.g3. The mainstream lines are heavily forcing and double-edged, with Black taking on c4 and breaking with ...c5 or ...e5.

white_ideas.idea: 5.Bg5 dxc4 and e4 with a big centre, or Qc2 and Bd3 against Meran set-ups
Pressure the c6/d5 centre and the queenside after Black takes on c4

black_ideas.idea: Take on c4 and play ...b5 for queenside space, or hit the centre with ...c5 and ...e5
Free the c8 bishop with ...b6/...Bb7 or ...b5 and ...Bb7

typical_structures.structure: Meran: Black pawns on b5/c6 against White d4/e4 centre
Anti-Moscow/Botvinnik: open centre with both sides ready to castle apart or sacrifice

character.notes: Main lines (Botvinnik, Meran, Moscow) are known for sharp theory and mutual tactical chances.

gambit.notes: Pawn on c4 is regained, no gambit.

structure.notes: QGD-like centre with tension; flexible, resolving to semi-open.

approach.notes: Standard theory; a core reply to the Queen's Gambit.

level.notes: Deep forcing theory in the Botvinnik and Meran lines.

sublines_that_differ.name: Botvinnik Variation
sublines_that_differ.how: Very sharp and forcing, tactical and sacrificial.

character.reason: Main lines are forcing and double-edged in the Botvinnik and Moscow.

gambit.reason: Pawns are exchanged, not given up for good.

structure.reason: Centre stays in tension in most lines, with open play after ...dxc4.

approach.reason: A main-line reply to the Queen's Gambit.

level.reason: Long forcing theory in the main lines.
